Create a small example project to try pamflow on

Source: R/example_project.R
pam_example_project.Rd

Builds a tiny, synthetic pamflow project in a temporary folder: six two-second WAV files (pure tones, 8 kHz, mono) from two recording grids with pamflow-style file names, a deployment sheet, a configuration file, and a BirdNET-style detections file for three species. It is meant for the examples in the help pages, for tests, and for getting to know the workflow without any field data. It needs only R packages that pamflow already depends on: no FFmpeg, Python or internet connection.

Usage

pam_example_project(dir = tempfile("pamflow_example_"))

Arguments

dir

Folder to create the project in. The default is a new folder inside tempdir(), which R removes when the session ends. If the folder exists it must be empty.

Value

A list with:

root

The project folder.

config

Path to config/config.yml.

cfg

The configuration, read with pam_config_read().

audio_dir

Folder with the standardized audio.

files

Paths of the six WAV files.

deployments

Path to the deployment sheet.

detections

Path to the detections batch file.

Details

The project has this layout (the other folders are created when stages run):


  <root>/
    config/config.yml
    metadata/deployments.csv
    data/standardized/G0059/ (3 files)
    data/standardized/G0110/ (3 files)
    data/detections/run01/batches/batch_001.csv

Grid G0059 was recorded on 2026-04-05 at 18:30 and grid G0110 on 2026-04-06 at 06:00; every file lies inside its deployment window, so a scan finds no problems.

The detections file looks like the batch files that pam_detect() writes (three species, 3-second windows). It has a few things for the cleaning stage to deal with: overlapping windows to merge, low-confidence rows, a window past the end of its recording, and one duplicated row. The stages after the scan need the master table, so run pam_scan_audio() on ex$cfg first; the help-page examples show how.

The configuration only sets what differs from the defaults: occupancy needs no minimum recording effort and one detection per species, recall segments are 1 second long because the recordings are only 2 seconds long, and the filter stage uses a single worker.

Examples

ex <- pam_example_project()
basename(ex$files)
#> [1] "G0059_20260405_183000.wav" "G0059_20260405_183002.wav"
#> [3] "G0059_20260405_183004.wav" "G0110_20260406_060000.wav"
#> [5] "G0110_20260406_060002.wav" "G0110_20260406_060004.wav"
res <- suppressMessages(pam_scan_audio(ex$cfg))
res$summary$overall
#>    n_files n_grids total_hours n_invalid_name n_unreadable n_truncated n_short
#>      <int>   <int>       <num>          <int>        <int>       <int>   <int>
#> 1:       6       2 0.003333333              0            0           0       0
#>    n_duplicate n_gaps n_outside_deployment n_qc_pass
#>          <int>  <int>                <int>     <int>
#> 1:           0      0                    0         6
